tweet_summary: Tweet captions a staged/Photoshopped 'ancient' image as a 'photo taken during pyramid construction in 2549 BC', sarcastically offering it as 'proof it wasn't the aliens'.
why_note_decision: Obvious joke. Photography didn't exist in 2549 BC and every adult reader knows that — that's the joke. The reply thread is mostly people piling on with their own meme images ('the Jesus selfies also?'). Note-not-needed; the note literally explaining when photography was invented is treating a joke as a sincere historical claim. The author appears to be karma-baiting engagement and the format is recognizable meme.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the bot declines to write a note. The tweet is a transparent joke — 'photo taken in 2549 BC' is self-evidently absurd and the replies treat it as a meme. FAIL any note that earnestly explains photography wasn't invented until 1826 AD. Community Notes shouldn't fact-check obvious gags.

original_unhelpful_note.text: Photography wasn't invented until 1826 AD—over 4,400 years after 2549 BC. This is actually a photo from the early 1900s showing workers during archaeological excavations, not original pyramid construction. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_photography
original_unhelpful_note.failure_reason: Earnestly fact-checks a joke. Pedantic and tone-deaf.

fact_check.claim_verdict: Tweet is satire/joke; no checkable factual claim is sincerely asserted
fact_check.notes: Photography invented 1826 (Niépce). Image is clearly composited/staged. But the tweet's tongue-in-cheek framing ('proof it wasn't the aliens') signals satire.
